issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify addGuestStudents(int) (a single-parameter method), but the template declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with an extra boolean parameter. The solution implements addGuestStudents(int). This parameter mismatch will confuse students and cause compilation/test failures because the template signature does not match the expected API.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to match the specification and solution: change to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and remove the boolean parameter (or alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to document the boolean parameter if that was intended).

issues.description: The problem statement and solution specify an addGuestStudents(int) method (single int parameter), but the template Lecture.java declares a different signature addGuestStudents(int, boolean). This parameter-name/signature mismatch refers to the same conceptual operation (adding guest students) with different identifiers/signature across artifacts, which will confuse students and cause mapping/tests to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: replace public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (or provide an overloaded single-argument version) and update the stub implementation accordingly so students clearly map the task to the template.
